title: Tokens Are the Cheap Part — Steve Jamison, Jellyfish
talk_summary: The talk argues that AI token spend should be judged against delivered merged PRs, not in isolation, because salary/oversight dominates cost and heavier token use correlated with more throughput and lower cost per PR. It recommends tracking cost per merged PR alongside throughput and quality counterweights like reverts, while watching for diminishing returns.

takeaways.technique: Cost per merged PR, not token bill
takeaways.what_they_do: They combine AI spend with human salary/oversight into a single cost-per-merged-PR metric and track it monthly beside throughput and quality.
takeaways.evidence_quote: AI is about 2 and 1/2% of the cost to produce another unit of merged code.
takeaways.numbers: AI ~2.5% of cost per merged PR; salary ~97.5%

takeaways.technique: Route by cost per merged PR
takeaways.what_they_do: They compare token-spend groups against merged-PR throughput and cost per PR, finding heavier spend can still lower total delivery cost.
takeaways.evidence_quote: More tokens leads to more PRs, which leads to a lower cost of delivery.
takeaways.numbers: Top 10% used 8x median tokens but had 25% lower cost per PR; heavy spenders saw 67% throughput gain vs ~40%

takeaways.what_they_do: They track reverts and quality metrics beside AI spend and PR throughput so speed gains are not mistaken for quality gains.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Watch reverts and quality metrics beside all of this as a counterweight.
takeaways.numbers: Revert-rate deltas were slightly below noise; no severe quality issue observed at higher token spend

takeaways.what_they_do: They plot token usage against cost per PR and use the curve to show large early gains followed by diminishing but still positive returns.
takeaways.evidence_quote: There's a steep drop at the beginning where relative small AI spend results in large gains initially.
takeaways.numbers: Top 10% spent 8x tokens for 25% lower cost per PR vs median

takeaways.what_they_do: They compare the same developer’s heavy-token weeks with their own low-token weeks to isolate the effect of more AI usage.
takeaways.evidence_quote: They spend about twice as much on tokens, merged 27% more PRs
takeaways.numbers: 2x tokens; 27% more merged PRs; ~18% lower cost per PR

takeaways.what_they_do: They verify throughput gains are not from smaller PRs; AI tends to increase lines changed per PR, which stresses review.
takeaways.evidence_quote: AI is driving an increase in line level lines of code generated per PR.
takeaways.numbers: Throughput gains were not driven by smaller PRs
